name: Pelet
who: A man of Judah, son of Jahdai, listed among the descendants of Caleb.
key: The sons of Jahdai were Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph (1 Chronicles 2).
Jahdai's family is listed among the descendants of Caleb, brother of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Peleth
who: A man of Judah, son of Jonathan, in the line of Jerahmeel.
key: The sons of Jonathan were Peleth and Zaza (1 Chronicles 2).
These were the descendants of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Peninnah
who: A wife of Elkanah who had children and provoked his childless wife Hannah year after year.
key: Elkanah had two wives, and Peninnah had children while Hannah had none (1 Samuel 1).
At the yearly sacrifice in Shiloh, Elkanah gave portions to Peninnah and her children (1 Samuel 1).

name: Peter
who: Galilean fisherman, brother of Andrew, who became a leading apostle of Jesus and preached at Pentecost.
key: Jesus called him from his fishing nets to follow him (Matthew 4).
He confessed Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God (Matthew 16).

name: Pethuel
who: The father of Joel, the prophet who called Judah to repent after a locust plague.
key: The word of the LORD came to Joel son of Pethuel (Joel 1).
His son Joel described a devastating locust plague and called Judah to lament (Joel 1).

name: Palti
who: Son of Laish of Gallim, to whom Saul gave David's wife Michal, and who wept when she was taken back.
key: Saul gave his daughter Michal, David's wife, to Palti son of Laish, of Gallim (1 Samuel 25).
Ish-bosheth took Michal from her husband Paltiel son of Laish at David's demand (2 Samuel 3).

name: Pharaoh Neco
who: A king of Egypt who killed King Josiah at Megiddo and then controlled Judah's throne.
key: He marched toward the Euphrates, and King Josiah was killed opposing him at Megiddo (2 Kings 23).
He warned Josiah that God had sent him, but Josiah would not listen (2 Chronicles 35).

name: Pharaoh
who: The unnamed king of Egypt who took Sarai into his household when Abram went to Egypt during a famine.
key: Pharaoh's officials praised Sarai, and she was taken into his house, believed to be Abram's sister (Genesis 12).
Pharaoh treated Abram well for her sake, giving him livestock and servants (Genesis 12).

name: Pharaoh
who: The king of Egypt in Joseph's day, who made Joseph ruler over Egypt and welcomed Jacob's family.
key: He imprisoned his chief cupbearer and baker, who met Joseph in prison (Genesis 40).
Joseph interpreted his dreams, and he set Joseph over all Egypt (Genesis 41).

name: Pharaoh
who: The king of Egypt who enslaved the Israelites and ordered their newborn sons to be killed.
key: A new king who did not know Joseph enslaved Israel with hard labor (Exodus 1).
He ordered the Hebrew midwives to kill newborn boys, but they feared God (Exodus 1).

name: Pharaoh
who: The king of Egypt at the exodus, who refused to free Israel until God struck Egypt with plagues.
key: When Moses and Aaron asked him to let Israel go, he made their labor harder (Exodus 5).
He hardened his heart as God sent plague after plague on Egypt (Exodus 7–10).

name: Pharaoh
who: King of Egypt in Solomon's day, who gave his daughter to Solomon in marriage.
key: Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh and married his daughter (1 Kings 3).
Pharaoh captured Gezer and gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife (1 Kings 9).

name: Pharaoh
who: The king of Egypt in Hezekiah's day, whose help Judah sought against the Assyrians.
key: The Assyrian commander mocked trust in Pharaoh as leaning on a broken reed (2 Kings 18).
Isaiah declared that the wise counselors of Pharaoh gave foolish counsel (Isaiah 19).

name: Pharaoh
who: The king of Egypt named among the rulers who must drink the cup of the LORD's wrath in Jeremiah's prophecy.
key: Jeremiah's prophecy of the cup is dated to Jehoiakim's fourth year, Nebuchadnezzar's first (Jeremiah 25).
Pharaoh king of Egypt, his officials, and his people are named among the nations to drink it (Jeremiah 25).

name: Pharaoh Hophra
who: The king of Egypt in Zedekiah's day, named Hophra by Jeremiah, whose downfall Jeremiah and Ezekiel announced.
key: Jeremiah announced that Pharaoh Hophra would be given into his enemies' hands (Jeremiah 44).
Ezekiel condemned Zedekiah for breaking his oath and seeking help from Egypt (Ezekiel 17).

name: Perez
who: Son of Judah and Tamar, twin of Zerah, and ancestor of King David and Jesus.
key: He was born a twin, breaking out ahead of his brother Zerah (Genesis 38).
He went down to Egypt with Jacob's household (Genesis 46).

name: Philemon
who: A believer whose house hosted a church and to whom Paul wrote, appealing for his slave Onesimus.
key: Paul greeted Philemon as a beloved fellow worker, with the church meeting in his house (Philemon 1).
Paul thanked God for Philemon's love and faith, which refreshed the hearts of the saints (Philemon 1).

name: Philetus
who: A false teacher whom Paul named with Hymenaeus for saying the resurrection had already happened.
key: Paul warned that the talk of Hymenaeus and Philetus would spread like gangrene (2 Timothy 2).
They swerved from the truth, saying the resurrection had already happened (2 Timothy 2).

name: Philip
who: One of the twelve apostles, from Bethsaida, who brought Nathanael to Jesus.
key: Jesus called him to follow, and he brought Nathanael to Jesus (John 1).
He is listed among the twelve apostles (Matthew 10).

name: Philip
who: A brother of Herod Antipas and the husband of Herodias before Antipas took her as his wife.
key: Herod had imprisoned John because of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife (Matthew 14).
John had told Herod it was not lawful to have his brother's wife (Mark 6).

name: Philip
who: One of the seven chosen to serve the Jerusalem church, later known as Philip the evangelist.
key: He was chosen as one of the seven to oversee the daily distribution (Acts 6).
He proclaimed Christ in Samaria, and many believed and were baptized (Acts 8).

name: Phinehas
who: Priest, son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron, known for his zeal for the LORD.
key: He killed Zimri and Cozbi, stopping the plague, and received a covenant of perpetual priesthood (Numbers 25).
He went with Israel's army against Midian, carrying the holy vessels and trumpets (Numbers 31).

name: Phinehas
who: A son of Eli who served as a priest at Shiloh but treated the Lord's offering with contempt.
key: He and his brother Hophni served as priests of the Lord at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1).
The brothers took sacrifices wrongly, lay with women at the tabernacle, and ignored their father (1 Samuel 2).

name: Pontius Pilate
who: Roman governor of Judea who sentenced Jesus to be crucified.
key: He governed Judea when John the Baptist began his ministry (Luke 3).
He questioned Jesus about being king of the Jews and found no guilt in him (John 18).

name: Piram
who: A king of Jarmuth who joined four other Amorite kings against Gibeon and was defeated by Joshua.
key: Adoni-zedek of Jerusalem asked Piram to join an attack on Gibeon for making peace with Israel (Joshua 10).
Joshua defeated the five kings, who hid in a cave at Makkedah and were then executed (Joshua 10).

name: Pithon
who: A son of Micah and great-grandson of Jonathan, listed in the genealogy of King Saul's family.
key: Pithon is listed first among the sons of Micah, son of Merib-baal, in Saul's line (1 Chronicles 8).
The genealogy of Saul's descendants is repeated, again naming Pithon (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Porcius Festus
who: The Roman governor of Judea who succeeded Felix and heard Paul's case, sending him to Caesar.
key: He succeeded Felix as governor while Paul remained in custody (Acts 24).
He heard Paul at Caesarea, and Paul appealed to Caesar rather than go to Jerusalem (Acts 25).

name: Potiphar
who: An Egyptian officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, who bought Joseph as a slave.
key: Potiphar bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites who had brought him to Egypt (Genesis 39).
Seeing the LORD was with Joseph, he put him in charge of his whole household (Genesis 39).

name: Priscilla
who: A Jewish Christian woman who, with her husband Aquila, worked and ministered alongside Paul.
key: Expelled from Rome under Claudius, she and Aquila welcomed Paul in Corinth as fellow tentmakers (Acts 18).
She and Aquila explained the way of God more accurately to Apollos in Ephesus (Acts 18).

name: Puah
who: A Hebrew midwife in Egypt who, with Shiphrah, feared God and refused Pharaoh's order to kill Hebrew baby boys.
key: Pharaoh ordered Puah and Shiphrah to kill every Hebrew boy at birth (Exodus 1).
Fearing God, the midwives let the boys live and gave Pharaoh an explanation (Exodus 1).

name: Puah
who: A man of Issachar, son of Dodo and father of Tola, who judged Israel after Abimelech.
key: Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel (Judges 10).
His son lived at Shamir in Ephraim's hill country and judged Israel twenty-three years (Judges 10).

name: Publius
who: The chief official of Malta, who welcomed Paul after his shipwreck and whose father Paul healed.
key: Publius welcomed Paul and his companions and hosted them for three days (Acts 28).
Paul prayed for Publius's father, sick with fever and dysentery, and healed him (Acts 28).

name: Queen of Sheba
who: Foreign queen who traveled to Jerusalem to test Solomon's wisdom and praised the LORD for him.
key: Hearing of Solomon's fame, she came to test him with hard questions (1 Kings 10).
Overwhelmed by his wisdom and court, she blessed the LORD who set Solomon on Israel's throne (1 Kings 10).

name: Raamah
who: A son of Cush and grandson of Ham, whose sons Sheba and Dedan are listed in the Table of Nations.
key: Raamah is named among the sons of Cush, son of Ham (Genesis 10).
He fathered Sheba and Dedan (Genesis 10).

name: Rabshakeh
who: High-ranking Assyrian official sent by Sennacherib to demand Jerusalem's surrender.
key: Sennacherib sent him with a great army to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem (2 Kings 18).
He mocked Judah's trust in the LORD and in Egypt (2 Kings 18).

name: Rachel
who: Laban's younger daughter, Jacob's beloved wife, and mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
key: Rachel met Jacob at a well while watering her father's sheep (Genesis 29).
Jacob served Laban seven years for her, but Laban first gave him Leah (Genesis 29).

name: Rahab
who: A prostitute of Jericho who hid Israel's spies and was spared when the city fell.
key: She hid two Israelite spies on her roof and sent the king's men away (Joshua 2).
She confessed that the Lord is God in heaven above and on earth (Joshua 2).

name: Ram
who: A son of Hezron from Judah, the father of Amminadab and an ancestor of David and Jesus.
key: He is listed in the line from Perez to David (Ruth 4).
He is named among the sons of Hezron in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Ram
who: A man of Judah, the firstborn son of Jerahmeel, named in Chronicles' genealogy of Judah.
key: Ram is named as the firstborn of Jerahmeel, who was Hezron's firstborn son (1 Chronicles 2).
His sons were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Ram
who: Ancestor of the family to which Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, Job's young counselor, belonged.
key: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, burned with anger at Job (Job 32).
This descendant of Ram spoke only after Job's three older friends had no answer (Job 32).

name: Reaiah
who: A Reubenite in the line of Joel, son of Micah and father of Baal.
key: The sons of Joel are traced through Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaiah, and Baal (1 Chronicles 5).
The line continued to Beerah, a Reubenite chief whom Tiglath-pileser of Assyria carried into exile (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Rebekah
who: Daughter of Bethuel, wife of Isaac, and mother of Esau and Jacob.
key: Abraham's servant found Rebekah at a well when she watered his camels (Genesis 24).
She agreed to go with him and became Isaac's wife (Genesis 24).

name: Rechab
who: A Benjaminite raiding captain from Beeroth who, with his brother Baanah, murdered Saul's son Ish-bosheth.
key: Rechab and his brother Baanah, sons of Rimmon of Beeroth, led raiding bands for Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 4).
They entered Ish-bosheth's house at midday, killed him on his bed, and beheaded him (2 Samuel 4).

name: Rechab
who: The father of Jonadab and the ancestor of the Rechabites.
key: His son Jehonadab joined Jehu in his zeal against the worship of Baal (2 Kings 10).
His son Jonadab commanded his descendants not to drink wine and to live in tents (Jeremiah 35).

name: Rechab
who: The father of Malchijah, the district ruler who repaired Jerusalem's Dung Gate in Nehemiah's day.
key: His son Malchijah ruled the district of Beth-haccherem (Nehemiah 3).
Malchijah rebuilt the Dung Gate, setting its doors, bolts, and bars (Nehemiah 3).

name: Regem
who: A man of Judah, son of Jahdai, listed among the descendants of Caleb.
key: The sons of Jahdai were Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph (1 Chronicles 2).
Jahdai's family is listed among the descendants of Caleb, brother of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Rehabiah
who: A Levite, the only son of Moses' son Eliezer, whose descendants became very numerous.
key: Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very many (1 Chronicles 23).
Isshiah was the chief among the sons of Rehabiah (1 Chronicles 24).

name: Rehob
who: The father of Hadadezer, the king of Zobah in Syria whom David defeated.
key: David defeated Rehob's son Hadadezer, king of Zobah, in battle (2 Samuel 8).
David took Hadadezer's gold shields and much bronze to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 8).

name: Rehoboam
who: Son of Solomon and first king of Judah after the kingdom divided.
key: Rehoboam went to Shechem to be made king over all Israel (1 Kings 12).
He rejected the elders' advice, and the northern tribes followed Jeroboam instead (1 Kings 12).

name: Rehum
who: A leader among the exiles who returned from Babylon to Judah with Zerubbabel.
key: Rehum was among the leaders who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
A Rehum was among the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10).

name: Rehum
who: A commander in the province Beyond the River who wrote to Artaxerxes against Jerusalem and halted its rebuilding.
key: Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes (Ezra 4).
They warned that if the city were rebuilt, it would stop paying tribute (Ezra 4).

name: Rehum
who: One of the chiefs of the people who set their seal on the covenant in Nehemiah's day.
key: After confessing their sins, the returned exiles made a firm written covenant (Nehemiah 9).
Rehum was among the chiefs of the people who sealed it (Nehemiah 10).

name: Remaliah
who: The father of Pekah, who seized the throne of Israel; Isaiah refers to Pekah simply as Remaliah's son.
key: Pekah son of Remaliah conspired against King Pekahiah and reigned over Israel in Samaria (2 Kings 15).
Pekah son of Remaliah killed a great number of Judah's soldiers in one day (2 Chronicles 28).

name: Reu
who: A descendant of Shem, the son of Peleg and the father of Serug.
key: He fathered Serug at thirty-two and lived 239 years in all (Genesis 11).
He is listed in the line from Shem to Abraham (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Reuben
who: Firstborn son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Reuben.
key: He was born to Leah, the first of Jacob's sons (Genesis 29).
He slept with his father's concubine Bilhah (Genesis 35).

name: Reuel
who: A son of Esau by Basemath and ancestor of chiefs in Edom.
key: He was born to Esau and Basemath in the land of Canaan (Genesis 36).
His sons Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah became chiefs in Edom (Genesis 36).

name: Reumah
who: The concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and mother of four of his sons.
key: Abraham heard news of his brother Nahor's family, including his concubine Reumah (Genesis 22).
She bore Nahor four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah (Genesis 22).

name: Rezin
who: King of Syria at Damascus who allied with Pekah of Israel against King Ahaz of Judah.
key: The LORD began sending Rezin and Pekah against Judah (2 Kings 15).
Rezin and Pekah besieged Ahaz in Jerusalem but could not conquer him (2 Kings 16).

name: Rezon
who: A Syrian leader who seized Damascus and became an adversary of Israel throughout Solomon's reign.
key: Rezon son of Eliada fled from his master Hadadezer, king of Zobah (1 Kings 11).
After David defeated Zobah, he gathered men around him and led a raiding band (1 Kings 11).

name: Rhoda
who: A servant girl in the Jerusalem house of Mary, mother of John Mark, who answered Peter's knock.
key: After an angel freed Peter from prison, Rhoda came to answer his knock at the gate (Acts 12).
Recognizing Peter's voice, in her joy she ran in to tell the others without opening the gate (Acts 12).

name: Rimmon
who: A Benjaminite of Beeroth whose sons Baanah and Rechab murdered Saul's son Ish-bosheth.
key: Rimmon of Beeroth, a Benjaminite, was the father of Baanah and Rechab, raiding captains for Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 4).
His sons killed Ish-bosheth as he lay on his bed and brought his head to David (2 Samuel 4).

name: Riphath
who: A grandson of Japheth through Gomer, named in the table of nations after the flood.
key: Riphath is listed as a son of Gomer, son of Japheth, in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among Gomer's sons, with Ashkenaz and Togarmah (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Rizpah
who: A concubine of King Saul who kept watch over the bodies of her executed sons.
key: Rizpah daughter of Aiah was a concubine of King Saul (2 Samuel 3).
Ish-bosheth accused Abner of sleeping with her, and the angry Abner turned to support David (2 Samuel 3).

name: Rufus
who: A son of Simon of Cyrene, the man compelled to carry Jesus' cross.
key: Mark names Rufus and his brother Alexander as sons of Simon of Cyrene (Mark 15).
Their father Simon was forced by the soldiers to carry Jesus' cross (Mark 15).

name: Ruth
who: A Moabite widow who stayed loyal to Naomi, married Boaz, and became the great-grandmother of King David.
key: After her husband died, she refused to leave Naomi and committed herself to Naomi's God (Ruth 1).
She gleaned barley in the field of Boaz, who showed her protective kindness (Ruth 2).

name: Sabtah
who: A son of Cush and grandson of Ham, named in the table of nations after the flood.
key: Sabtah is listed as a son of Cush, son of Ham, in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among the sons of Cush (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Shelah
who: Descendant of Shem and father of Eber, listed in the line from Noah to Abraham and in Jesus' genealogy.
key: He is listed among Shem's descendants as the father of Eber (Genesis 10).
He fathered Eber at thirty and lived 403 years more (Genesis 11).

name: Sallu
who: A Benjaminite, son of Meshullam, who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile.
key: Sallu son of Meshullam is listed among the Benjaminites who lived in Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chronicles 9).
His ancestry is traced through Meshullam and Hodaviah to Hassenuah (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Sallu
who: A Benjaminite, son of Meshullam, who settled in Jerusalem in Nehemiah's day.
key: Sallu son of Meshullam is named first among the Benjaminites who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11).
His ancestry is traced through Meshullam, Joed, and Pedaiah back to Jeshaiah (Nehemiah 11).

name: Salmon
who: The son of Nahshon and father of Boaz, an ancestor of King David and Jesus.
key: He is listed in the line from Perez to David (Ruth 4).
He appears in Judah's genealogy as the father of Boaz (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Samson
who: A Nazirite from the tribe of Dan whom God empowered to judge Israel against the Philistines.
key: The angel of the Lord announced Samson's birth to Manoah's wife (Judges 13).
He married a Philistine woman of Timnah and posed a riddle at the feast (Judges 14).

name: Samuel
who: Prophet, priest, and last judge of Israel, who anointed both Saul and David as king.
key: Born in answer to Hannah's prayer, he was dedicated to serve the Lord at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1).
As a boy, he heard the Lord call him by name at night (1 Samuel 3).

name: Sanballat
who: Sanballat the Horonite, a leading opponent of Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.
key: He was displeased that Nehemiah came to seek the welfare of Israel, and mocked the work (Nehemiah 2).
He ridiculed the builders and plotted with others to attack Jerusalem (Nehemiah 4).

name: Sapphira
who: Wife of Ananias in the early Jerusalem church; both died after lying about money from land they sold.
key: With her husband Ananias she sold property and knowingly kept back part of the price (Acts 5).
About three hours after Ananias died, Peter asked her the sale price, and she lied (Acts 5).

name: Sarah
who: Wife of Abraham who, though barren into old age, bore the promised son Isaac.
key: Abram's wife Sarai was barren and had no child (Genesis 11).
She gave her servant Hagar to Abram to bear a child for her (Genesis 16).

name: Satan
who: The adversary of God and his people, who tempts, accuses, and deceives, and whose final defeat Scripture foretells.
key: He accused Job before the Lord and was allowed to test him (Job 1–2).
He incited David to take a census of Israel (1 Chronicles 21).

name: Saul
who: Son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin, anointed by Samuel as Israel's first king.
key: Samuel anointed Saul, who was later chosen by lot as king (1 Samuel 10).
He offered a sacrifice himself instead of waiting for Samuel, and was rebuked (1 Samuel 13).

name: Sceva
who: A Jewish chief priest whose seven sons tried to cast out an evil spirit in Jesus' name at Ephesus.
key: Sceva was a Jewish chief priest whose seven sons were traveling exorcists in Ephesus (Acts 19).
His sons tried to cast out an evil spirit in the name of the Jesus whom Paul preached (Acts 19).

name: Seba
who: A son of Cush and grandson of Ham, named in the table of nations after the flood.
key: Seba is listed first among the sons of Cush, son of Ham, in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among the sons of Cush (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Secundus
who: A believer from Thessalonica who accompanied Paul as he left Greece for Jerusalem.
key: Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians were among Paul's travel companions (Acts 20).
These companions went on ahead and waited for Paul at Troas (Acts 20).

name: Segub
who: Youngest son of Hiel of Bethel, who died when his father set up the gates of rebuilt Jericho.
key: Joshua had declared that whoever rebuilt Jericho would set its gates at the cost of his youngest son (Joshua 6).
Hiel set up Jericho's gates at the cost of his youngest son Segub, in Ahab's day (1 Kings 16).

name: Segub
who: A man of Judah, son of Hezron by the daughter of Machir, and father of Jair of Gilead.
key: At sixty, Hezron married the daughter of Machir, father of Gilead, and she bore Segub (1 Chronicles 2).
Segub fathered Jair, who held twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Seir
who: Seir the Horite, ancestor of the people who lived in the land of Edom before Esau's descendants.
key: Seir the Horite's sons are listed as the inhabitants of the land before Esau's descendants (Genesis 36).
His sons Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan became Horite chiefs (Genesis 36).

name: Sennacherib
who: King of Assyria who invaded Judah and besieged Jerusalem during Hezekiah's reign.
key: He captured Judah's fortified cities, and Hezekiah paid him tribute (2 Kings 18).
He sent the Rabshakeh to demand Jerusalem's surrender (2 Kings 18).

name: Serah
who: A daughter of Asher and granddaughter of Jacob, one of the few women named in Israel's genealogies.
key: Serah, daughter of Asher, is listed among Jacob's family who went down to Egypt (Genesis 46).
She is named again in the census of Asher's clans on the plains of Moab (Numbers 26).

name: Seraiah
who: The chief priest of Judah when Jerusalem fell, executed by the king of Babylon at Riblah.
key: Nebuzaradan took Seraiah the chief priest captive when Jerusalem fell (2 Kings 25).
He was brought to the king of Babylon at Riblah and put to death (2 Kings 25).

name: Seraiah
who: An army captain of Judah, son of Tanhumeth, who joined Governor Gedaliah at Mizpah after Jerusalem fell.
key: After Babylon destroyed Jerusalem, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth was among the captains still in the field (2 Kings 25).
He and other captains came to Gedaliah at Mizpah when Babylon appointed him governor (2 Kings 25).

name: Seraiah
who: A man of Judah, son of Kenaz and brother of Othniel, Israel's first judge.
key: Chronicles lists Othniel and Seraiah as the sons of Kenaz in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 4).
Seraiah fathered Joab, the father of Ge-harashim, a settlement of craftsmen (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Seraiah
who: A man of the tribe of Simeon, son of Asiel, whose grandson Jehu was a clan chief.
key: Seraiah son of Asiel is named in Simeon's genealogy as grandfather of Jehu, a chief (1 Chronicles 4).
In Hezekiah's days these Simeonite chiefs took pastureland near Gedor and settled there (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Seraiah
who: A priest who returned from exile with Zerubbabel and whose name was carried on by a priestly family.
key: A Seraiah is named among the leaders who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
The name Seraiah heads the priests who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's day (Nehemiah 10).

name: Seraiah
who: An officer of King Jehoiakim, son of Azriel, sent to arrest Jeremiah and Baruch.
key: After burning Jeremiah's scroll, Jehoiakim ordered Seraiah son of Azriel and others to seize Baruch and Jeremiah (Jeremiah 36).
They could not find them, for the LORD had hidden them (Jeremiah 36).

name: Seraiah
who: A royal staff officer, brother of Baruch, who carried Jeremiah's prophecy against Babylon to that city.
key: Seraiah son of Neriah was quartermaster when he went with King Zedekiah to Babylon (Jeremiah 51).
Jeremiah gave him a book of the disasters coming on Babylon, to read aloud there (Jeremiah 51).

name: Sergius Paulus
who: The Roman proconsul of Cyprus who believed after hearing Barnabas and Saul preach.
key: Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man, was proconsul of Cyprus at Paphos (Acts 13).
He summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God (Acts 13).

name: Serug
who: A descendant of Shem, the son of Reu and the father of Nahor.
key: He fathered Nahor at thirty and lived 230 years in all (Genesis 11).
He is listed in the line from Shem to Abraham (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Seth
who: Son of Adam and Eve, born after Abel's murder, through whom the line to Noah continued.
key: Eve bore Seth, saying God had appointed another offspring in place of Abel (Genesis 4).
After his son Enosh was born, people began to call on the LORD's name (Genesis 4).

name: Shaaph
who: A man of Judah, son of Jahdai, listed among the descendants of Caleb.
key: The sons of Jahdai were Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph (1 Chronicles 2).
Jahdai's family is listed among the descendants of Caleb, brother of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Shadrach
who: One of Daniel's three Judean friends in Babylon, kept safe by God in the fiery furnace.
key: Taken to Babylon, he was renamed Shadrach and avoided the king's food (Daniel 1).
He prayed with Daniel for God to reveal the king's dream (Daniel 2).

name: Shallum
who: A king of Israel who seized the throne by assassination and reigned only one month.
key: Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against King Zechariah of Israel, killed him, and took the throne (2 Kings 15).
Zechariah's death fulfilled the LORD's word that Jehu's dynasty would last four generations (2 Kings 15).

name: Shallum
who: The keeper of the wardrobe in King Josiah's day and husband of the prophetess Huldah.
key: Hilkiah and the king's officials went to Huldah, wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, keeper of the wardrobe (2 Kings 22).
Chronicles also names Huldah as the wife of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe (2 Chronicles 34).

name: Shallum
who: A priest in Zadok's line and father of Hilkiah, the high priest in King Josiah's day.
key: Chronicles places Shallum between Zadok and Hilkiah in the high-priestly line (1 Chronicles 6).
He is called Meshullam in the list of priests who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Shallum
who: A Korahite Levite, son of Kore, who was chief of the gatekeepers at the house of the Lord.
key: Shallum was chief of the gatekeepers stationed at the king's gate on the east (1 Chronicles 9).
He and his Korahite kinsmen guarded the thresholds of the tent (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Shallun
who: Ruler of the district of Mizpah who rebuilt Jerusalem's Fountain Gate in Nehemiah's day.
key: Shallun son of Col-hozeh ruled the district of Mizpah when Jerusalem's wall was rebuilt (Nehemiah 3).
He rebuilt the Fountain Gate, roofing it and setting its doors, bolts, and bars (Nehemiah 3).

name: Shemariah
who: A son of King Rehoboam by Mahalath, a granddaughter of David.
key: Mahalath bore Rehoboam sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham (2 Chronicles 11).
Rehoboam later made Maacah's son Abijah chief prince among his brothers (2 Chronicles 11).

name: Shamgar
who: A deliverer of Israel after Ehud, who struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad.
key: After Ehud, Shamgar son of Anath killed six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad (Judges 3).
By this he also saved Israel (Judges 3).

name: Shammah
who: A grandson of Esau through Reuel, and a chief among the Edomites.
key: Shammah was a son of Reuel, Esau's son by Basemath (Genesis 36).
He became one of the chiefs of Edom descended from Reuel (Genesis 36).

name: Shammah
who: Son of Agee the Hararite, one of David's three foremost warriors, who held a lentil field against the Philistines.
key: Shammah son of Agee the Hararite was one of David's three chief mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
When Israel's troops fled from the Philistines, he took his stand in a field full of lentils (2 Samuel 23).

name: Shammah
who: Shammah of Harod, one of David's thirty mighty men.
key: Shammah of Harod is listed among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Chronicles lists him as Shammoth of Harod among David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11).

name: Shammah
who: The third son of Jesse and an older brother of King David.
key: Samuel saw Shammah, but the Lord had not chosen him as king (1 Samuel 16).
He followed Saul to battle against the Philistines with his two older brothers (1 Samuel 17).

name: Shammai
who: A man of Judah in the line of Jerahmeel, son of Onam and father of Nadab and Abishur.
key: Shammai and his brother Jada are listed as the sons of Onam (1 Chronicles 2).
Shammai's sons were Nadab and Abishur (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Shaphan
who: Secretary to King Josiah who read the newly found Book of the Law to the king.
key: Josiah sent Shaphan to the temple to arrange payment for repairs (2 Kings 22).
Hilkiah gave Shaphan the Book of the Law, and he read it to Josiah (2 Kings 22).

name: Shaphat
who: The father of the prophet Elisha, from Abel-meholah.
key: God told Elijah to anoint Elisha son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah as prophet after him (1 Kings 19).
Elisha left his oxen, kissed his father and mother goodbye, and followed Elijah (1 Kings 19).

name: Shaphat
who: A descendant of David's royal line after the exile, one of the sons of Shemaiah.
key: The sons of Shemaiah were Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat, six (1 Chronicles 3).
Shemaiah was the son of Shecaniah, in the royal line of Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Shaul
who: A Kohathite Levite, son of Uzziah, named in Chronicles' genealogy of Kohath's descendants.
key: Chronicles lists Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul in succession among Kohath's descendants (1 Chronicles 6).
Kohath's line produced Heman, a singer David put in charge of the service of song (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Shealtiel
who: A son of Jehoiachin, the captive king of Judah, and father of Zerubbabel, who led the return from exile.
key: He is listed among the sons of Jeconiah the captive (1 Chronicles 3).
His son Zerubbabel helped rebuild the altar of the God of Israel (Ezra 3).

name: Sheba
who: A son of Raamah and great-grandson of Ham, named in the table of nations after the flood.
key: Sheba is listed as a son of Raamah, son of Cush, in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him with his brother Dedan among Raamah's sons (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Sheba
who: A son of Joktan in the line of Shem, named in the table of nations after the flood.
key: Sheba is listed among the thirteen sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem through Eber (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among Joktan's sons (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Sheba
who: A grandson of Abraham and Keturah, son of Jokshan and brother of Dedan.
key: Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave gifts to his sons by his concubines and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).

name: Sheba
who: Benjaminite son of Bichri who led a revolt against King David and was beheaded at Abel of Beth-maacah.
key: He blew a trumpet, declaring Israel had no portion in David, and Israel followed him (2 Samuel 20).
Joab pursued him and besieged him in the city of Abel of Beth-maacah (2 Samuel 20).

name: Sheba
who: A Gadite, one of the seven sons of Abihail who headed fathers' houses in Gilead and Bashan.
key: Abihail's sons Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber headed their fathers' houses (1 Chronicles 5).
These Gadites lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and in the pasturelands of Sharon (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Shebna
who: A royal secretary under King Hezekiah of Judah during the Assyrian siege of Jerusalem.
key: He went out with Eliakim and Joah to meet the Assyrian Rabshakeh at Jerusalem's wall (2 Kings 18).
Hezekiah sent him with Eliakim and the senior priests to seek the prophet Isaiah (2 Kings 19).

name: Shebna
who: A steward over the royal household in Jerusalem whom Isaiah said God would remove and replace with Eliakim.
key: Shebna was the steward over the royal household in Jerusalem (Isaiah 22).
Isaiah rebuked him for carving out a grand tomb for himself (Isaiah 22).

name: Shecaniah
who: A man of the family of Elam, son of Jehiel, who urged Ezra to lead the people in a covenant of repentance.
key: Shecaniah son of Jehiel confessed that the people had broken faith by marrying foreign women (Ezra 10).
He said there was still hope for Israel and proposed a covenant with God (Ezra 10).

name: Shechem
who: Hivite prince, son of Hamor, who violated Jacob's daughter Dinah.
key: Jacob bought land near the city from the sons of Hamor (Genesis 33).
He seized and violated Dinah, then asked to marry her (Genesis 34).

name: Shechem
who: A descendant of Manasseh through Gilead and ancestor of the Shechemite clan.
key: Shechem son of Gilead headed the clan of the Shechemites in Manasseh's census (Numbers 26).
His clan received an inheritance among the tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan (Joshua 17).

name: Shedeur
who: A man of Reuben whose son Elizur led the tribe during Israel's wilderness journey.
key: His son Elizur was named to help Moses take the census for Reuben (Numbers 1).
Elizur son of Shedeur led Reuben's camp on the south side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Shelah
who: The third son of Judah by the daughter of Shua, and ancestor of the Shelanite clan.
key: He was born to Judah and the daughter of Shua at Chezib (Genesis 38).
Judah withheld him from marrying the widowed Tamar, fearing he too would die (Genesis 38).

name: Shelemiah
who: The father of Hananiah, who helped repair Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah.
key: His son Hananiah repaired another section of Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3).
Hananiah son of Shelemiah worked alongside Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph (Nehemiah 3).

name: Shelomoth
who: A Gershonite Levite, son of Shimei, listed among family heads when David organized the Levites.
key: When David organized the Levites, Shelomoth was listed among the sons of Shimei (1 Chronicles 23).
He and his brothers Haziel and Haran were heads of fathers' houses of Ladan (1 Chronicles 23).

name: Shelomoth
who: A Levite descended from Moses' son Eliezer, who oversaw the treasuries of gifts dedicated to the LORD.
key: Eliezer's line ran through Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, and Zichri to Shelomoth (1 Chronicles 26).
Shelomoth and his brothers oversaw the gifts dedicated by David and his army commanders (1 Chronicles 26).

name: Shelomith
who: A Levite, chief of the sons of Izhar, listed when David organized the Levites.
key: The sons of Izhar were led by Shelomith the chief (1 Chronicles 23).
Among the Izharites, Shelomoth is listed with his son Jahath (1 Chronicles 24).

name: Shelumiel
who: The son of Zurishaddai and chief of the tribe of Simeon during the wilderness years.
key: Shelumiel was appointed to help Moses take the census for Simeon (Numbers 1).
He led Simeon's camp on the south side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Shem
who: Son of Noah who survived the flood and became ancestor of Abraham and the Israelites.
key: He entered the ark with Noah and his family (Genesis 7).
He and Japheth covered their father's nakedness and were blessed by Noah (Genesis 9).

name: Shema
who: A Benjaminite family head in Aijalon who, with Beriah, put the inhabitants of Gath to flight.
key: Beriah and Shema were heads of fathers' houses of the inhabitants of Aijalon (1 Chronicles 8).
They caused the inhabitants of Gath to flee (1 Chronicles 8).

name: Shemaiah
who: A man of God and prophet in Judah during the reign of King Rehoboam.
key: Shemaiah told Rehoboam not to fight against Israel, and the people obeyed (1 Kings 12).
Chronicles repeats this word of the Lord forbidding war with their brothers (2 Chronicles 11).

name: Shemaiah
who: A descendant of David's royal line after the exile, son of Shecaniah and father of Neariah and his brothers.
key: The son of Shecaniah was Shemaiah (1 Chronicles 3).
The sons of Shemaiah were Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat, six (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Shemaiah
who: A Reubenite in the line of Joel, son of Joel and father of Gog.
key: The sons of Joel are traced through Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaiah, and Baal (1 Chronicles 5).
The line continued to Beerah, a Reubenite chief whom Tiglath-pileser of Assyria carried into exile (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Shemaiah
who: A man hired by Nehemiah's enemies to frighten him into hiding in the temple.
key: Nehemiah visited Shemaiah son of Delaiah, who was confined to his home (Nehemiah 6).
Shemaiah urged Nehemiah to hide in the temple, claiming men were coming to kill him (Nehemiah 6).

name: Shemaiah
who: Shemaiah of Nehelam, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon who opposed Jeremiah.
key: Shemaiah of Nehelam prophesied to the exiles in Babylon, though the LORD had not sent him (Jeremiah 29).
He wrote to the priest Zephaniah, urging him to put Jeremiah in the stocks (Jeremiah 29).

name: Shemeber
who: The king of Zeboiim in Abraham's day, one of the kings of the valley who rebelled against Chedorlaomer.
key: Shemeber king of Zeboiim joined the kings of the valley in rebelling against Chedorlaomer (Genesis 14).
The four eastern kings defeated them in the Valley of Siddim and carried off Lot from Sodom (Genesis 14).

name: Shemer
who: The owner of the hill of Samaria, which King Omri bought to build Israel's new capital.
key: King Omri bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver (1 Kings 16).
Omri built a city on the hill and named it Samaria after Shemer (1 Kings 16).

name: Shephatiah
who: A Benjaminite, son of Reuel, whose son Meshullam headed a father's house in Jerusalem after the exile.
key: Meshullam son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah, is listed among Jerusalem's Benjaminites (1 Chronicles 9).
All these men were heads of fathers' houses (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Shepho
who: A son of Shobal and grandson of Seir the Horite, named among the early inhabitants of Edom.
key: Shepho is listed as a son of Shobal, son of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats him among Shobal's sons (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Sherebiah
who: A Levite of good understanding who returned with Ezra and helped teach the Law to the people.
key: Sherebiah, a man of discretion, joined Ezra's group with his sons and kinsmen (Ezra 8).
Ezra entrusted him with others to carry the silver and gold for the temple (Ezra 8).

name: Sheshai
who: One of the three sons of Anak, a clan of giants living at Hebron when Israel entered Canaan.
key: The twelve spies saw Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, descendants of Anak, at Hebron (Numbers 13).
Caleb drove the three sons of Anak out of Hebron (Joshua 15).

name: Shimei
who: Benjaminite of Saul's clan, son of Gera, who cursed David during Absalom's rebellion.
key: He cursed David and threw stones as David fled Jerusalem (2 Samuel 16).
David refused to let Abishai kill him (2 Samuel 16).

name: Shimei
who: A Reubenite in the line of Joel, son of Gog and father of Micah.
key: The sons of Joel are traced through Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaiah, and Baal (1 Chronicles 5).
The line continued to Beerah, a Reubenite chief whom Tiglath-pileser of Assyria carried into exile (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Shimei
who: A son of Gershon and grandson of Levi, ancestor of the Levite clan of the Shimeites.
key: He is listed with his brother Libni as a son of Gershon (Exodus 6).
His descendants formed the Shimeite clan among the Gershonites (Numbers 3).

name: Shimshai
who: A scribe in the Persian province Beyond the River who, with Rehum, opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem.
key: Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote to Artaxerxes against Jerusalem (Ezra 4).
Artaxerxes replied to Rehum and Shimshai, ordering the work on the city to stop (Ezra 4).

name: Shiphrah
who: One of two Hebrew midwives in Egypt who feared God and refused Pharaoh's order to kill Israelite baby boys.
key: Pharaoh ordered Shiphrah and Puah, Hebrew midwives, to kill every Hebrew baby boy at birth (Exodus 1).
They feared God and let the boys live (Exodus 1).

name: Shishak
who: A king of Egypt who sheltered Jeroboam and later invaded Judah.
key: Jeroboam fled to Shishak in Egypt to escape Solomon (1 Kings 11).
In Rehoboam's fifth year he attacked Jerusalem and took the temple and palace treasures (1 Kings 14).

name: Shitrai
who: Shitrai of Sharon, the official in charge of King David's herds that grazed in Sharon.
key: Shitrai the Sharonite was over the herds that pastured in Sharon (1 Chronicles 27).
He was among the stewards who managed King David's property (1 Chronicles 27).

name: Shobach
who: Commander of Hadadezer's Syrian army, killed when David defeated the Syrians at Helam.
key: Hadadezer brought out the Syrians beyond the Euphrates, with Shobach commanding his army (2 Samuel 10).
David crossed the Jordan and fought the Syrians at Helam (2 Samuel 10).

name: Shobal
who: A son of Seir the Horite and one of the Horite chiefs in the land of Seir.
key: Shobal is listed among the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land (Genesis 36).
His sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam (Genesis 36).

name: Shobi
who: An Ammonite from Rabbah, son of Nahash, who brought supplies to David during Absalom's revolt.
key: Shobi son of Nahash came from Rabbah of the Ammonites (2 Samuel 17).
When David fled from Absalom to Mahanaim, Shobi, Machir, and Barzillai brought beds, utensils, and food (2 Samuel 17).

name: Shua
who: A daughter of Heber in the tribe of Asher, named in Chronicles' genealogy.
key: Shua was the daughter of Heber, a grandson of Asher (1 Chronicles 7).
She is named with her brothers Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Shuah
who: A son of Abraham by Keturah, sent away eastward with his brothers.
key: Keturah bore Abraham Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave gifts to his concubines' sons and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).

name: Sibbecai
who: A Hushathite warrior among David's mighty men who killed a descendant of the giants.
key: Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, a descendant of the giants (2 Samuel 21).
He is listed among the mighty men of David's army (1 Chronicles 11).

name: Sihon
who: King of the Amorites at Heshbon, defeated by Israel east of the Jordan.
key: Sihon refused Israel passage and attacked them, but Israel defeated him (Numbers 21).
Moses recalled that the Lord hardened Sihon's spirit and gave his land to Israel (Deuteronomy 2).

name: Silas
who: Leader in the Jerusalem church who became Paul's missionary companion.
key: He was chosen to carry the Jerusalem council's letter to Antioch, then joined Paul (Acts 15).
He and Paul were beaten and jailed in Philippi, then freed by an earthquake (Acts 16).

name: Simeon
who: Jacob's second son by Leah and ancestor of the tribe of Simeon.
key: Leah named him Simeon because the Lord heard she was unloved (Genesis 29).
With Levi, he killed the men of Shechem after Dinah was violated (Genesis 34).

name: Simeon
who: A righteous man in Jerusalem who held the infant Jesus in the temple and praised God for his salvation.
key: Simeon was a righteous, devout man in Jerusalem, waiting for the consolation of Israel (Luke 2).
The Holy Spirit had revealed he would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ (Luke 2).

name: Simon the Zealot
who: One of the twelve apostles, called the Zealot or the Cananaean to distinguish him from Simon Peter.
key: Matthew lists him among the twelve apostles as Simon the Cananaean (Matthew 10).
Mark also names him among the Twelve whom Jesus appointed (Mark 3).

name: Simon
who: One of the brothers of Jesus, named by the people of Nazareth when they took offense at him.
key: The people of Nazareth named Simon among Jesus' brothers, with James, Joseph, and Judas (Matthew 13).
Knowing his family, they took offense at Jesus, who did few mighty works there (Mark 6).

name: Simon the leper
who: A man of Bethany, known as Simon the leper, at whose home Jesus was anointed shortly before his death.
key: Shortly before the Passover, Jesus was at the home of Simon the leper in Bethany (Matthew 26).
There a woman poured costly ointment on Jesus, who said she had prepared his body for burial (Mark 14).

name: Simon of Cyrene
who: A man from Cyrene whom Roman soldiers compelled to carry Jesus' cross to the crucifixion.
key: As Jesus was led out to be crucified, soldiers compelled Simon of Cyrene to carry his cross (Matthew 27).
Mark notes he was coming in from the country and was the father of Alexander and Rufus (Mark 15).

name: Simon Iscariot
who: Father of Judas Iscariot, the disciple who betrayed Jesus; he is known only through his son.
key: Jesus said one of the Twelve was a devil, meaning Judas the son of Simon Iscariot (John 6).
The devil put it into the heart of Judas, Simon's son, to betray Jesus (John 13).

name: Simon
who: A magician in Samaria who believed Philip's preaching but tried to buy the power to give the Holy Spirit.
key: Simon practiced magic in Samaria and amazed the people, who called him the great power of God (Acts 8).
Under Philip's preaching he believed, was baptized, and followed Philip, astonished at the signs (Acts 8).

name: Simon
who: A tanner in Joppa whose house by the sea hosted the apostle Peter.
key: Peter stayed many days in Joppa at the house of Simon the tanner (Acts 9).
An angel told Cornelius to send for Peter, who was lodging with Simon by the sea (Acts 10).

name: Sippai
who: A Philistine warrior descended from the giants, killed by Sibbecai in David's wars.
key: Sippai, a descendant of the giants, fought for the Philistines against David's army (2 Samuel 21).
Sibbecai the Hushathite killed him at Gezer, and the Philistines were subdued (1 Chronicles 20).

name: Sisera
who: Commander of King Jabin's Canaanite army, defeated by Barak and killed by Jael.
key: With 900 iron chariots he oppressed Israel for twenty years (Judges 4).
The LORD routed his army before Barak, and he fled on foot (Judges 4).

name: Solomon
who: Son of David and Bathsheba who succeeded David as king, famed for wisdom and for building the temple.
key: Born to David and Bathsheba, he was also named Jedidiah by the Lord through Nathan (2 Samuel 12).
He was anointed king to succeed his father David (1 Kings 1).

name: Sopater
who: A believer from Berea, son of Pyrrhus, who accompanied Paul as he left Greece for Jerusalem.
key: Sopater of Berea, son of Pyrrhus, accompanied Paul as he returned through Macedonia (Acts 20).
His companions included Aristarchus, Secundus, Gaius of Derbe, Timothy, Tychicus, and Trophimus (Acts 20).

name: Sosthenes
who: The ruler of the synagogue in Corinth who was beaten in front of Gallio's tribunal.
key: After Gallio dismissed the case against Paul, the crowd seized Sosthenes, the synagogue ruler (Acts 18).
They beat him in front of the tribunal, but Gallio paid no attention (Acts 18).

name: Stephanas
who: A believer in Corinth whose household were the first converts in Achaia and devoted themselves to serving the saints.
key: Paul personally baptized the household of Stephanas in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1).
His household were the first converts in Achaia and devoted themselves to serving the saints (1 Corinthians 16).

name: Stephen
who: One of the seven chosen to serve the Jerusalem church, and the first Christian martyr.
key: He was chosen among the seven, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit (Acts 6).
Opponents who could not withstand his wisdom brought false charges before the council (Acts 6).

name: Syntyche
who: A Christian woman at Philippi who had labored beside Paul in the gospel.
key: Paul urged Euodia and Syntyche to agree with each other in the Lord (Philippians 4).
He asked a true companion to help these women, who had contended at his side for the gospel (Philippians 4).

name: Tahath
who: A Kohathite Levite, son of Assir and father of Uriel, in the ancestry of the singer Heman.
key: Chronicles lists Assir, Tahath, and Uriel in succession among Kohath's descendants (1 Chronicles 6).
Heman's ancestry names Zephaniah son of Tahath, son of Assir (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Tahpenes
who: A queen of Egypt, wife of the Pharaoh who sheltered Hadad the Edomite in Solomon's day.
key: Pharaoh gave the sister of his wife Queen Tahpenes in marriage to Hadad the Edomite (1 Kings 11).
Tahpenes herself weaned Hadad's son Genubath, who grew up among Pharaoh's sons in the palace (1 Kings 11).

name: Talmai
who: One of the three sons of Anak, a giant clan living at Hebron when Israel entered Canaan.
key: The twelve spies saw Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, descendants of Anak, living at Hebron (Numbers 13).
Caleb drove the three sons of Anak, including Talmai, out of Hebron (Joshua 15).

name: Talmai
who: King of Geshur, father of David's wife Maacah and grandfather of Absalom.
key: His daughter Maacah married David and bore Absalom at Hebron (2 Samuel 3).
After killing Amnon, Absalom fled to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur (2 Samuel 13).

name: Talmon
who: A Levite gatekeeper whose family guarded the gates of the house of God before and after the exile.
key: Talmon was among the gatekeepers who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9).
His descendants were among the gatekeepers who returned from Babylon (Ezra 2).

name: Tamar
who: The daughter-in-law of Judah who bore him the twins Perez and Zerah.
key: She married Judah's son Er, and after his death his brother Onan (Genesis 38).
When Judah withheld Shelah, she disguised herself and conceived by Judah (Genesis 38).

name: Tamar
who: A daughter of King David and full sister of Absalom, who was violated by her half brother Amnon.
key: Amnon tricked her into his room, forced her, and then sent her away in disgrace (2 Samuel 13).
She lived desolate in Absalom's house, and Absalom later had Amnon killed (2 Samuel 13).

name: Tanhumeth
who: The father of Seraiah, an army captain of Judah who came to Governor Gedaliah at Mizpah.
key: Seraiah son of Tanhumeth was among the captains who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah (2 Kings 25).
Gedaliah swore to these captains that serving the king of Babylon would go well with them (Jeremiah 40).

name: Tarshish
who: A son of Javan and great-grandson of Noah through Japheth, listed in the Table of Nations.
key: Tarshish is listed among the sons of Javan, from whom the coastland peoples spread (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats his name among the descendants of Japheth (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Tebah
who: A son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by his concubine Reumah.
key: Abraham was told that Nahor's concubine Reumah bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah (Genesis 22).
These sons are listed after the eight sons Milcah bore to Nahor (Genesis 22).

name: Teman
who: Esau's grandson, the eldest son of Eliphaz, and a chief in Edom.
key: Teman is listed first among the sons of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn (Genesis 36).
He became one of the chiefs descended from Esau in the land of Edom (Genesis 36).

name: Teman
who: A chief of Edom listed among Esau's chiefs by their clans and regions.
key: Teman is named among the chiefs of Esau, listed by families and regions (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats him among the chiefs of Edom (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Terah
who: Father of Abraham, Nahor, and Haran, who led his family from Ur toward Canaan.
key: He fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran (Genesis 11).
He took Abram, Sarai, and Lot from Ur toward Canaan but settled in Haran (Genesis 11).

name: Tertullus
who: A lawyer who brought the Jewish leaders' charges against Paul before Governor Felix.
key: Tertullus came to Caesarea with the high priest Ananias and elders to accuse Paul (Acts 24).
He flattered Felix and charged Paul with stirring riots, leading the Nazarene sect, and profaning the temple (Acts 24).

name: Theophilus
who: The honored reader to whom Luke addressed both his Gospel and the book of Acts.
key: Luke wrote an orderly account for most excellent Theophilus, so he might know the certainty of what he was taught (Luke 1).
Luke addressed Acts to Theophilus too, recalling his first book about all Jesus began to do and teach (Acts 1).

name: Thomas
who: One of the twelve apostles, called the Twin, remembered for doubting and then confessing the risen Jesus.
key: He was named among the twelve apostles Jesus sent out (Matthew 10).
When Jesus went to Lazarus, Thomas urged the disciples to go and die with him (John 11).

name: Tikvah
who: Father of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe and husband of the prophetess Huldah in Josiah's day.
key: Josiah's officials went to Huldah, wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas (2 Kings 22).
Chronicles calls him Tokhath son of Hasrah (2 Chronicles 34).

name: Tiglath-pileser
who: A king of Assyria who invaded Israel and took many Israelites into exile.
key: In Pekah's reign he captured cities of Naphtali and carried the people to Assyria (2 Kings 15).
Ahaz sent him tribute; he captured Damascus and killed King Rezin (2 Kings 16).

name: Timaeus
who: The father of Bartimaeus, the blind beggar whom Jesus healed near Jericho.
key: Bartimaeus, son of Timaeus, sat begging by the road as Jesus left Jericho (Mark 10).
Jesus restored his son's sight, and Bartimaeus followed him on the way (Mark 10).

name: Timna
who: The concubine of Esau's son Eliphaz and mother of Amalek, ancestor of the Amalekites.
key: Timna, concubine of Esau's son Eliphaz, bore him Amalek (Genesis 36).
Chronicles also records Amalek as born to Eliphaz by Timna (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Timothy
who: A young believer from Lystra who became Paul's trusted coworker and the recipient of two letters.
key: Paul took Timothy, son of a Jewish believer and a Greek father, on his travels (Acts 16).
Paul sent him to strengthen churches such as Thessalonica and Corinth (1 Thessalonians 3; 1 Corinthians 4).

name: Tirhakah
who: King of Cush whose army marched out against the Assyrian king Sennacherib during Hezekiah's reign.
key: Sennacherib heard that Tirhakah king of Cush had set out to fight against him (2 Kings 19).
Sennacherib then sent messengers again to threaten Hezekiah, and Hezekiah spread the letter before the LORD (Isaiah 37).

name: Tiria
who: A man of Judah, son of Jehallelel, named in the tribe's genealogy.
key: Tiria is listed among the sons of Jehallelel, with Ziph, Ziphah, and Asarel (1 Chronicles 4).
His family appears among the clans of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Tirzah
who: One of the five daughters of Zelophehad of Manasseh, who inherited land because their father had no sons.
key: Tirzah was one of Zelophehad's five daughters, since he had no sons (Numbers 26).
With her sisters she asked Moses for their father's inheritance, and the Lord granted it (Numbers 27).

name: Titus
who: A Greek believer and trusted coworker of Paul, entrusted with ministry in Corinth and Crete.
key: He went with Paul to Jerusalem and was not compelled to be circumcised (Galatians 2).
Paul had no rest in Troas because he did not find Titus there (2 Corinthians 2).

name: Tobiah
who: An Ammonite official who repeatedly opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.
key: He and Sanballat were displeased that someone had come to seek Israel's welfare (Nehemiah 2).
He mocked the wall, saying even a fox would break it down (Nehemiah 4).

name: Togarmah
who: A son of Gomer and descendant of Japheth, whose people became known for horses.
key: Togarmah is listed among the sons of Gomer, son of Japheth (Genesis 10).
Beth-togarmah traded horses, war horses, and mules for the wares of Tyre (Ezekiel 27).

name: Toi
who: King of Hamath who sent gifts and congratulations to David after David defeated Hadadezer.
key: Toi had been at war with Hadadezer king of Zobah, whom David defeated (2 Samuel 8).
He sent his son Joram to bless David, bringing articles of silver, gold, and bronze (2 Samuel 8).

name: Tola
who: A man of Issachar who judged Israel twenty-three years after the time of Abimelech.
key: After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah rose to save Israel, living at Shamir in Ephraim's hill country (Judges 10).
He judged Israel twenty-three years, then died, was buried in Shamir, and Jair followed him (Judges 10).

name: Trophimus
who: A Gentile believer from Ephesus who traveled with Paul.
key: Trophimus from the province of Asia accompanied Paul on his journey toward Jerusalem (Acts 20).
Jews who had seen him with Paul assumed Paul brought him into the temple, sparking a riot (Acts 21).

name: Tubal-cain
who: A son of Lamech and Zillah in Cain's line, the forger of instruments of bronze and iron.
key: Lamech's wife Zillah bore Tubal-cain, the forger of all instruments of bronze and iron (Genesis 4).
His sister was Naamah, and his half brothers Jabal and Jubal began herding and music (Genesis 4).

name: Tubal
who: A son of Japheth and grandson of Noah, whose descendants became a distant northern people.
key: He is listed among the sons of Japheth in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats his place among Japheth's sons (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Tychicus
who: A believer from Asia who traveled with Paul and carried his letters and news to the churches.
key: Tychicus of Asia accompanied Paul on his journey through Macedonia (Acts 20).
Paul sent him, a beloved brother and faithful minister, to share news with the Ephesians (Ephesians 6).

name: Uri
who: A man of Judah, son of Hur, whose son Bezalel was the chief craftsman of the tabernacle.
key: The Lord called Bezalel son of Uri by name to make the tabernacle (Exodus 31).
Moses announced that God had filled Uri's son Bezalel with skill (Exodus 35).

name: Uriah
who: A Hittite soldier among David's mighty men, husband of Bathsheba.
key: While Uriah was at war, David took his wife Bathsheba (2 Samuel 11).
Uriah refused to go home while the ark and army were in tents (2 Samuel 11).

name: Uriel
who: A Kohathite Levite, son of Tahath, named in Chronicles' genealogy of Kohath's descendants.
key: Chronicles lists Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul in succession among Kohath's descendants (1 Chronicles 6).
Heman's ancestry in the same chapter names Zephaniah son of Tahath at this point instead (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Uriah
who: A priest in Jerusalem under King Ahaz who built an altar from a pattern sent from Damascus.
key: Uriah built an altar copied from the model King Ahaz sent from Damascus (2 Kings 16).
At Ahaz's command he offered the regular sacrifices on the new altar (2 Kings 16).

name: Uzzah
who: A son of Abinadab who died when he touched the ark of God as David moved it.
key: He and his brother Ahio drove the new cart carrying the ark from Abinadab's house (2 Samuel 6).
When the oxen stumbled, he took hold of the ark, and God struck him dead (2 Samuel 6).

name: Uzzi
who: A priest descended from Aaron, listed in the high-priestly line and among Ezra's ancestors.
key: Uzzi son of Bukki is listed in the line of Aaron's son Eleazar, the father of Zerahiah (1 Chronicles 6).
Ezra's genealogy traces his priestly descent back through Uzzi to Aaron (Ezra 7).

name: Uzziah
who: A king of Judah, son of Amaziah, who reigned fifty-two years until pride brought leprosy.
key: Uzziah became king at sixteen and reigned fifty-two years (2 Chronicles 26).
As long as he sought the Lord, God made him prosper (2 Chronicles 26).

name: Uzziel
who: A Levite, son of Kohath and uncle of Moses and Aaron, whose descendants served at the tabernacle.
key: He is listed as a son of Kohath, and his sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri (Exodus 6).
Moses called his sons to carry away the bodies of Nadab and Abihu (Leviticus 10).

name: Uzziel
who: A Levite of Jeduthun's family who helped cleanse the temple under King Hezekiah.
key: Uzziel of the Jeduthunites was among the Levites who rose to serve when Hezekiah reopened the temple (2 Chronicles 29).
These Levites consecrated themselves and cleansed the house of the LORD as the king commanded (2 Chronicles 29).

name: Vashti
who: Queen of Persia, wife of King Ahasuerus, removed after refusing his summons during a royal feast.
key: She gave a feast for the women in King Ahasuerus's palace (Esther 1).
She refused the king's command to come and display her beauty before his guests (Esther 1).

name: Zabdi
who: A man of Judah, of the clan of Zerah, and grandfather of Achan.
key: Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, took some of the devoted things at Jericho (Joshua 7).
When lots were cast, the household of Zabdi was taken, and then Achan (Joshua 7).

name: Zacchaeus
who: A rich chief tax collector in Jericho who welcomed Jesus into his home and repented.
key: Being short, Zacchaeus climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus passing through Jericho (Luke 19).
Jesus called him down and stayed at his house, while the crowd grumbled (Luke 19).

name: Zechariah
who: King of Israel, son of Jeroboam II and last of Jehu's dynasty, who reigned six months in Samaria.
key: He succeeded his father Jeroboam II as king of Israel (2 Kings 14).
He did evil in the LORD's sight, as his fathers had done (2 Kings 15).

name: Zechariah
who: Priest and father of John the Baptist, made mute for doubting Gabriel's announcement of his son's birth.
key: He was a righteous priest of the division of Abijah, and his wife Elizabeth was barren (Luke 1).
Gabriel announced John's birth in the temple, and Zechariah was made mute for not believing (Luke 1).

name: Zechariah
who: Priest, son of Jehoiada, stoned in the temple court at King Joash's command for speaking God's word.
key: The Spirit of God came on him, and he warned Judah for forsaking the LORD (2 Chronicles 24).
At King Joash's command the people stoned him in the court of the LORD's house (2 Chronicles 24).

name: Zadok
who: A priest descended from Aaron who served King David and anointed Solomon king.
key: Zadok is listed with Ahimelech as a priest in David's government (2 Samuel 8).
During Absalom's revolt, David sent him back to Jerusalem with the ark (2 Samuel 15).

name: Zadok
who: A later priest in Aaron's high-priestly line, son of Ahitub and father of Shallum, and an ancestor of Ezra.
key: Zadok son of Ahitub is listed in the high-priestly line as the father of Shallum (1 Chronicles 6).
His descendant Azariah served as chief official of God's temple after the exile (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Zaham
who: A son of King Rehoboam by Mahalath, a granddaughter of David.
key: Mahalath bore Rehoboam sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham (2 Chronicles 11).
Rehoboam later made Maacah's son Abijah chief prince among his brothers (2 Chronicles 11).

name: Zalaph
who: Father of Hanun, who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah.
key: Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section of Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3).
Zalaph's son worked alongside Hananiah son of Shelemiah in the rebuilding (Nehemiah 3).

name: Zalmunna
who: King of Midian who, with Zebah, was pursued, captured, and executed by Gideon.
key: Gideon pursued Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian, across the Jordan (Judges 8).
The men of Succoth and Penuel refused bread to Gideon's pursuing troops (Judges 8).

name: Zaza
who: A man of Judah, son of Jonathan, in the line of Jerahmeel.
key: The sons of Jonathan were Peleth and Zaza (1 Chronicles 2).
These were the descendants of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Zebadiah
who: The son of Asahel, who succeeded his father as commander of David's army division for the fourth month.
key: His father Asahel, Joab's brother, commanded the division serving in the fourth month (1 Chronicles 27).
Zebadiah became commander of that division of 24,000 men after him (1 Chronicles 27).

name: Zebadiah
who: Son of Ishmael and ruler of the house of Judah, appointed over the king's matters under Jehoshaphat.
key: Jehoshaphat appointed judges in Jerusalem to decide disputes in the fear of the LORD (2 Chronicles 19).
Zebadiah was set over all matters of the king, while Amariah the chief priest handled the LORD's matters (2 Chronicles 19).

name: Zebadiah
who: A priest of the family of Immer who had married a foreign wife after the return from exile.
key: Zebadiah is listed among the descendants of Immer who had married foreign women (Ezra 10).
Under Ezra's reform, such men agreed to separate from their foreign wives (Ezra 10).

name: Zebah
who: King of Midian who, with Zalmunna, was pursued, captured, and executed by Gideon.
key: Gideon pursued Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian, across the Jordan (Judges 8).
The men of Succoth and Penuel refused bread to Gideon's pursuing troops (Judges 8).

name: Zebedee
who: A Galilean fisherman and the father of the apostles James and John.
key: His sons James and John left him in the boat to follow Jesus (Matthew 4).
He had hired servants who worked with him in the fishing boat (Mark 1).

name: Zebul
who: The ruler of the city of Shechem under Abimelech, who exposed Gaal's revolt.
key: Zebul, Abimelech's officer, governed the city of Shechem (Judges 9).
Angered by Gaal's boasting, he secretly sent messengers to warn Abimelech (Judges 9).

name: Zebulun
who: Sixth son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Zebulun.
key: He was born to Leah, who hoped her husband would now honor her (Genesis 30).
Jacob blessed him, saying he would dwell at the shore of the sea (Genesis 49).

name: Zechariah
who: A Levite gatekeeper, firstborn son of Meshelemiah, who served at the tent of meeting.
key: He was gatekeeper at the entrance of the tent of meeting (1 Chronicles 9).
He is named as the firstborn son of Meshelemiah among the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 26).

name: Zechariah
who: A man in Uzziah's day who instructed the king in the fear of God.
key: Uzziah sought God during the days of Zechariah, who instructed him in the fear of God (2 Chronicles 26).
As long as Uzziah sought the LORD, God gave him success (2 Chronicles 26).

name: Zechariah
who: A prophet after the exile, son of Berechiah and grandson of Iddo, who urged rebuilding the temple.
key: He and Haggai prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem (Ezra 5).
The elders finished the temple, prospering through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah (Ezra 6).

name: Zechariah
who: A family head of the descendants of Parosh who returned from Babylon with Ezra.
key: Zechariah of the descendants of Parosh was registered with 150 men in Ezra's company (Ezra 8).
The group traveled from Babylon to Jerusalem under God's protection (Ezra 8).

name: Zechariah
who: The son of Bebai, a family head who returned from Babylon with Ezra.
key: Zechariah son of Bebai was registered with 28 men in Ezra's company (Ezra 8).
The group traveled from Babylon to Jerusalem under God's protection (Ezra 8).

name: Zechariah
who: One of the leaders Ezra sent to recruit Levites for the journey from Babylon to Jerusalem.
key: Finding no Levites in the camp at the Ahava canal, Ezra summoned Zechariah and other leaders (Ezra 8).
They were sent to Iddo at Casiphia, and Levites and temple servants were brought to join the return (Ezra 8).

name: Zechariah
who: A descendant of Elam who had married a foreign wife after the return from exile.
key: Zechariah is listed among the descendants of Elam who had married foreign women (Ezra 10).
Under Ezra's reform, such men agreed to separate from their foreign wives (Ezra 10).

name: Zechariah
who: A descendant of Asaph, son of Jonathan, who blew a trumpet at the dedication of Jerusalem's rebuilt wall.
key: Zechariah son of Jonathan, descended from Asaph, was among the priests' sons with trumpets (Nehemiah 12).
His kinsmen, including Shemaiah, Judah, and Hanani, played the musical instruments of David (Nehemiah 12).

name: Zedekiah
who: Son of Josiah and the last king of Judah before Babylon destroyed Jerusalem.
key: Nebuchadnezzar made him king and changed his name from Mattaniah to Zedekiah (2 Kings 24).
He and Jerusalem's leaders broke their covenant to free their Hebrew slaves (Jeremiah 34).

name: Zedekiah
who: A false prophet, son of Chenaanah, who urged Ahab to battle and struck the prophet Micaiah.
key: Zedekiah made iron horns and prophesied that Ahab would push back the Syrians (1 Kings 22).
He struck Micaiah on the cheek for prophesying disaster (1 Kings 22).

name: Zedekiah
who: A false prophet among the exiles in Babylon, son of Maaseiah, condemned by Jeremiah.
key: The LORD said Zedekiah and Ahab son of Kolaiah were prophesying lies in his name (Jeremiah 29).
God announced Nebuchadnezzar would kill them, and their fate would become a curse among the exiles (Jeremiah 29).

name: Zeeb
who: One of the two Midianite princes captured and killed by the men of Ephraim during Gideon's victory.
key: The Ephraimites captured and killed Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb and brought his head to Gideon (Judges 7).
Gideon calmed Ephraim's anger, saying God had given Oreb and Zeeb into their hands (Judges 8).

name: Zelophehad
who: Manassite son of Hepher who died without sons, whose five daughters won the right to inherit.
key: He is listed as having no sons, only five daughters (Numbers 26).
His daughters asked Moses for their father's inheritance, and the LORD granted it (Numbers 27).

name: Zephaniah
who: A priest, son of Maaseiah, in Jerusalem during King Zedekiah's reign.
key: Zedekiah sent him to Jeremiah to inquire of the Lord about Nebuchadnezzar (Jeremiah 21).
He read to Jeremiah a letter from Shemaiah demanding Jeremiah be confined (Jeremiah 29).

name: Zephaniah
who: A prophet in the days of King Josiah who warned of the day of the LORD.
key: Zephaniah son of Cushi, a descendant of Hezekiah, prophesied during Josiah's reign (Zephaniah 1).
He announced the coming day of the LORD against Judah's idolatry and complacency (Zephaniah 1).

name: Zepho
who: Esau's grandson, a son of Eliphaz, and a chief in Edom.
key: Zepho is listed among the sons of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn (Genesis 36).
He became one of the chiefs descended from Esau in Edom (Genesis 36).

name: Zerah
who: A son of Judah and Tamar, twin brother of Perez, and ancestor of the Zerahite clan.
key: At his birth a scarlet thread was tied on his hand, but his twin Perez came out first (Genesis 38).
He went down to Egypt with the family of Jacob (Genesis 46).

name: Zerah
who: Esau's grandson through Reuel and a chief in Edom.
key: Zerah is listed among the sons of Reuel, Esau's son by Basemath (Genesis 36).
He became one of the chiefs descended from Reuel in the land of Edom (Genesis 36).

name: Zerah
who: A man of Bozrah whose son Jobab became king of Edom.
key: When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned as king of Edom (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats the record of Jobab son of Zerah among Edom's kings (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Zerah
who: A Cushite commander whose vast army was defeated by King Asa of Judah.
key: Zerah the Cushite marched against Judah with a huge army and chariots, reaching Mareshah (2 Chronicles 14).
Asa cried to the LORD for help, and the LORD struck down the Cushites, who fled toward Gerar (2 Chronicles 14).

name: Zerah
who: A son of Simeon who went down to Egypt with Jacob and founded the Zerahite clan.
key: Listed as Zohar, he went down to Egypt with Jacob among the sons of Simeon (Genesis 46).
He is named among the clans of Simeon in the genealogy of Moses and Aaron (Exodus 6).

name: Zerahiah
who: A priest descended from Aaron through Eleazar and Phinehas, listed in the high-priestly genealogy.
key: Chronicles lists Zerahiah son of Uzzi in the line from Aaron to the exile (1 Chronicles 6).
His line continued through his son Meraioth toward Zadok (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Zerahiah
who: Father of Eliehoenai, who led two hundred men of the family of Pahath-moab back with Ezra.
key: Of the sons of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah came with two hundred men (Ezra 8).
They returned from Babylonia with Ezra in the reign of King Artaxerxes (Ezra 8).

name: Zeresh
who: The wife of Haman, who first urged him to build a gallows for Mordecai.
key: Zeresh and Haman's friends advised building a gallows fifty cubits high to hang Mordecai (Esther 5).
After Haman's humiliation, she warned that he would surely fall before Mordecai the Jew (Esther 6).

name: Zeror
who: A Benjaminite ancestor of King Saul, son of Becorath and father of Abiel.
key: Zeror son of Becorath is named in the Benjaminite family line of Kish (1 Samuel 9).
His grandson Kish became the father of Saul, Israel's first king (1 Samuel 9).

name: Zeruah
who: A widow of Ephraim, the mother of Jeroboam, the first king of the northern kingdom.
key: Zeruah, a widow, was the mother of Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah (1 Kings 11).
Her son rebelled against Solomon and later became king over the ten northern tribes (1 Kings 12).

name: Zerubbabel
who: A descendant of David and governor of Judah who led exiles home and rebuilt the temple.
key: Zerubbabel led exiles from Babylon back to Jerusalem and Judah (Ezra 2).
With Jeshua he rebuilt the altar and laid the temple foundation (Ezra 3).

name: Zeruiah
who: David's sister and mother of his commanders Joab, Abishai, and Asahel.
key: Zeruiah and Abigail are listed as sisters of David and his brothers (1 Chronicles 2).
Her sons are usually named as the sons of Zeruiah (1 Samuel 26; 2 Samuel 2).

name: Zetham
who: A Gershonite Levite of Ladan's family who helped oversee the temple treasuries.
key: Zetham is listed among the sons of Ladan when David organized the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).
Zetham and his brother Joel were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26).

name: Zethan
who: A Benjaminite, son of Bilhan, whose family was counted among Benjamin's mighty warriors.
key: The sons of Bilhan were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar (1 Chronicles 7).
They were heads of fathers' houses, mighty warriors, 17,200 able to go to war (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Zia
who: A Gadite, one of the seven sons of Abihail who headed fathers' houses in Gilead and Bashan.
key: Abihail's sons Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber headed their fathers' houses (1 Chronicles 5).
These Gadites lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and in the pasturelands of Sharon (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Ziba
who: A servant of Saul's household whom David appointed to farm the land restored to Mephibosheth.
key: He told David about Jonathan's son Mephibosheth and was put in charge of his land (2 Samuel 9).
He met the fleeing David with supplies and accused Mephibosheth of disloyalty, receiving his property (2 Samuel 16).

name: Zibeon
who: A Hivite, grandfather of Esau's wife Oholibamah through his son Anah.
key: Esau married Oholibamah, daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite (Genesis 36).
Oholibamah bore Esau three sons, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah (Genesis 36).

name: Zibeon
who: A son of Seir the Horite, one of the Horite chiefs, and the grandfather of Esau's wife Oholibamah.
key: Esau's wife Oholibamah was the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon (Genesis 36).
Zibeon is listed among the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land (Genesis 36).

name: Zichri
who: A Levite of the Kohathite clan, son of Izhar and brother of Korah.
key: Zichri is listed among the sons of Izhar, a son of Kohath, in Levi's genealogy (Exodus 6).
His brother Korah later led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16).

name: Zichri
who: A Benjaminite whose son Joel was overseer of the Benjaminites living in Jerusalem after the exile.
key: His son Joel was overseer of the Benjaminites who lived in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11).
Judah son of Hassenuah served as second over the city under Joel son of Zichri (Nehemiah 11).

name: Zillah
who: One of the two wives of Lamech, Cain's descendant, and mother of Tubal-cain and Naamah.
key: Lamech took two wives, Adah and Zillah (Genesis 4).
Zillah bore Tubal-cain, a forger of bronze and iron tools, and his sister Naamah (Genesis 4).

name: Zilpah
who: Leah's servant, given to Jacob as a wife, and mother of Gad and Asher.
key: Laban gave Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her servant (Genesis 29).
Leah gave her to Jacob, and she bore Gad and Asher (Genesis 30).

name: Zimran
who: A son of Abraham by Keturah, sent away to the east with his brothers.
key: Keturah bore Abraham Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave gifts to these sons and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).

name: Zimri
who: A Simeonite leader killed by Phinehas for flagrant sin with a Midianite woman during Israel's apostasy at Peor.
key: Zimri brought the Midianite woman Cozbi into his family in the sight of Moses and the weeping assembly (Numbers 25).
Phinehas killed both Zimri and Cozbi, and the plague on Israel stopped (Numbers 25).

name: Zimri
who: A chariot commander who assassinated King Elah and ruled Israel for only seven days.
key: He conspired against King Elah and killed him while Elah was drunk in Tirzah (1 Kings 16).
As king he struck down the entire house of Baasha, as the prophet Jehu had foretold (1 Kings 16).

name: Zimri
who: A Benjaminite descendant of King Saul through Jonathan, son of Jarah, also called Jehoaddah.
key: Jehoaddah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri, in the line of Saul through Jonathan (1 Chronicles 8).
Zimri fathered Moza, continuing the line of Saul's descendants (1 Chronicles 8).

name: Ziph
who: A man of Judah listed as a son of Jehallelel in the tribe's genealogy.
key: Ziph is named first among the sons of Jehallelel, with Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel (1 Chronicles 4).
Nothing more is recorded of him beyond Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Ziphah
who: A man of Judah, son of Jehallelel, listed in the tribe's genealogy.
key: Ziphah is named among the sons of Jehallelel, with Ziph, Tiria, and Asarel (1 Chronicles 4).
His family is recorded among the clans descended from Judah (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Zippor
who: The father of Balak, the king of Moab who hired Balaam to curse Israel.
key: His son Balak saw Israel's victories and feared them (Numbers 22).
Balaam addressed Balak as son of Zippor in his oracle of blessing (Numbers 23).

name: Zipporah
who: The Midianite wife of Moses, daughter of the priest Reuel (Jethro), and mother of Gershom and Eliezer.
key: After Moses defended Reuel's daughters at a well in Midian, Reuel gave him Zipporah as his wife (Exodus 2).
She bore Moses a son, Gershom (Exodus 2).

name: Zohar
who: A Hittite, father of Ephron, who sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah.
key: Abraham asked the Hittites to approach Ephron son of Zohar to sell him the cave of Machpelah (Genesis 23).
Isaac and Ishmael buried Abraham in that cave, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar (Genesis 25).

name: Zophar
who: Zophar the Naamathite, one of Job's three friends who came to comfort him and then accused him.
key: Zophar came with Eliphaz and Bildad to comfort Job and sat silently with him seven days (Job 2).
He rebuked Job's claims of innocence, saying God exacts less than Job's guilt deserves (Job 11).

name: Zuar
who: A man of Issachar whose son Nethanel led the tribe during Israel's wilderness journey.
key: His son Nethanel was named to help Moses take the census for Issachar (Numbers 1).
Nethanel son of Zuar led Issachar's camp on the east side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Zur
who: A Midianite chief whose daughter Cozbi was killed with Zimri by Phinehas at Peor.
key: Cozbi, killed with the Israelite Zimri by Phinehas, was the daughter of Zur (Numbers 25).
Zur was the head of the people of a father's house in Midian (Numbers 25).

name: Zurishaddai
who: A man of Simeon whose son Shelumiel led the tribe during Israel's wilderness journey.
key: His son Shelumiel was named to help Moses take the census for Simeon (Numbers 1).
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai led Simeon's camp on the south side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).
